label: Experientialism is an alternative to desirable-insofar-as-perfect
note: Positive rival account of what fixes desirability for lives of experiencing subjects: the experiential profile rather than perfection. Target: 060e7a1a's per-perfection biconditional as a whole; experientialism is compatible with each half alone (controls rows 2 and 3). Mechanism: comparison conjunct 3, given two lives with one profile differing in a perfection, the biconditional and experientialism are not jointly true; conjunct 2 gives the exact price (perfection supervenes on experience). Independent warrant offered for the rival (unread leads): the experience requirement, that what makes no difference to how a life is from the inside cannot make it go better for its subject (Mill, Utilitarianism ch. 4; Sumner; Crisp). The conflict holds only when 060e7a1a's DesirableIn is applied to lives of experiencing subjects.
